answer: No prior RBI approval is required when a private sector bank’s MD & CEO/CEO reaches 70 years; the regulation simply mandates that no person may continue in that role beyond 70 years, and the bank must retire the MD & CEO/CEO at that age. [S3]

The maximum interest rate a commercial bank may offer on deposits under the Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) Account Scheme is the rate payable on savings bank deposits held under the RFC Account Scheme. This is stated in the directions that the interest paid on conversion of FCNR(B) accounts to RFC/Resident Rupee accounts “shall not exceed the rate payable on savings bank deposits held under RFC Account Scheme”【S4】, and similarly for NRE deposits converted to RFC accounts the interest “shall be paid at a rate not exceeding the rate payable on savings deposits held in RFC accounts”【S1】.
A commercial bank must acknowledge a card complaint received by telephone within 30 days of receiving the complaint. [S3]
A public sector bank must appoint a majority of non‑executive directors (NEDs) to its Risk Management Committee. [S2]

An NBFC‑MFI must maintain a capital adequacy ratio of at least **15 %** of its aggregate risk‑weighted assets (S5).  As an “Other NBFC”, it is capped at a **maximum dividend payout ratio of 50 %** (S2).
